origin: The headline numbers, the unemployment rate and the June revision are accurate for the release. "3rd biggest monthly job loss since the pandemic" is not: on the fact-sheet list, four months since 2021 had larger declines than -23,000, which makes July the fifth largest (ranking computed by the case author; verified). "Expectations of +85,000" is within the spread of the surveys on the fact sheet, but no fetched source gives the +85,000 figure. The post's 4.2% unemployment expectation is unsourced on the fact sheet. Expected honest rating: 55 to 75.

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation, August 2026, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm. Published 2026-09-04. Also: "Local government education added 42,000 jobs in August, largely offsetting a decrease in the prior month."
